title: Taifa of Córdoba
capsule: The Taifa of Córdoba refers to the independent or semi-independent Muslim polity centered on Córdoba that emerged from the fragmentation of the Umayyad Caliphate; the dataset's attestation window of 1147–1250 places it in the period following the Almohad conquest of al-Andalus, when local governance again devolved from centralized Almohad authority. The earlier Córdoban taifa (1031–1091), governed by the Banu Jahwar under a uniquely collegial arrangement resembling a republic, had set a precedent of urban self-rule in the former caliphal capital. Córdoba's political history in this later window reflects the wider erosion of Almohad power, culminating in the Castilian conquest of the city by Ferdinand III on 29 June 1236, which permanently ended Muslim rule there.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent for the later Córdoban taifa period (post-1147) is poorly documented; the geometry in this dataset likely reflects approximate administrative zones rather than precisely bounded sovereignty.
